findings.title: A failed save destroys the pre-existing file at the target path (truncate-before-pickle, non-atomic write)
findings.description: save() opens fname with mode 'wb' (truncating any existing file to 0 bytes) BEFORE pickle.dump runs. If pickling then fails -- e.g. the object contains a lambda, generator, open file handle, thread lock, or a HyperAnimation (see F20-save-004) -- the user's previously saved good data at that path is irreversibly destroyed and a 0-byte corrupt stub is left behind. Verified: a 8152-byte good pickle went to 0 bytes and reload raised 'EOFError: Ran out of input'. Realistic trigger: a scientist re-saves an updated results dict that accidentally acquired an unpicklable member. Standard fix is an atomic write (dump to a temp file in the same directory, then os.replace), which also removes the corrupt-stub-on-new-path behavior.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
p = '/tmp/precious.pkl'
hyp.save(np.arange(1000.0), p)          # good file on disk
try:
    hyp.save(lambda x: x, p)            # fails mid-save
except Exception as e:
    print('save failed:', e)
hyp.load(p)                              # EOFError -- original data gone (file is 0 bytes)
findings.expected: A failed save leaves the previous file contents untouched (atomic write), or at minimum documents that the target is truncated before serialization.
findings.actual: save raised [AttributeError: Can't get local object 'destroys_existing.<locals>.<lambda>']; file size 8152 -> 0 bytes; file NO LONGER LOADS: EOFError: Ran out of input; original data intact: False

findings.title: save() silently ignores the file extension: data.csv/.npy/.mat/.xlsx/fig.png are all pickles, invalid in their nominal formats
findings.description: save() always writes a pickle regardless of extension, with no warning. hyp.load round-trips every such file EXACTLY (its b'\x80' byte-sniff rescues them), but the files are lies to every other tool: data.npy fails np.load ('ValueError: This file contains pickled (object) data'), data.csv fails pd.read_csv ('UnicodeDecodeError: ... byte 0x80 in position 0'), data.mat fails scipy.io.loadmat ('ValueError: Unknown mat file type, version 95, 117'), data.xlsx fails pd.read_excel, and hyp.save(fig, 'figure.png') produces a 'PNG' that plt.imread rejects ('SyntaxError: not a PNG file') -- even though the real figure exporter hyp.plot(..., save_path='fig.png') exists. This is asymmetric with hyp.load, which genuinely parses .npy/.npz/.csv/.tsv/.txt/.json/.parquet/.mat/.xlsx/.xls. A warning (or format dispatch, see F20-save-009) on recognized non-pickle extensions would prevent silently misleading files that scientists then hand to collaborators, Excel, or MATLAB.
findings.repro:
import pandas as pd, numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
df = pd.DataFrame({'a': [1.0, 2.0], 'b': [3.0, 4.0]})
hyp.save(df, '/tmp/data.csv')      # no warning
pd.read_csv('/tmp/data.csv')       # UnicodeDecodeError
hyp.save(df, '/tmp/data.npy')
np.load('/tmp/data.npy', allow_pickle=False)  # ValueError
findings.expected: Either format-aware writing keyed on extension (mirroring load), or a UserWarning that a pickle is being written under a non-pickle extension.
findings.actual: data.npy magic=b'\x80\x04\x95e' ... INVALID as .npy: ValueError: This file contains pickled (object) data. | data.csv ... UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0x80 in position 0 | data.mat ... ValueError: Unknown mat file type, version 95, 117 | figure.png: real PNG=False; plt.imread fails: SyntaxError: not a PNG file. All 17 files written as pickle bytes: True

findings.title: Round-trip silently returns the WRONG dataset when the saved filename collides with a dataset name (save(x,'iris') -> load('iris') = sklearn iris)
findings.description: save() writes to any bare filename, but load()'s resolution chain checks built-in example names and sklearn/seaborn dataset names BEFORE local files. Verified: after hyp.save(arr, 'iris') in the cwd, hyp.load('iris') silently returns scikit-learn's iris DataFrame, and after hyp.save(arr, 'weights'), hyp.load('weights') returns the hosted 36-subject fMRI dataset -- not the user's saved data. No error, no warning: silently wrong data. The shadowing is documented in load()'s docstring (and load('./iris') works, verified), but save()'s one-line docstring gives no hint, and save() could easily warn when fname (no path separator, no extension) matches a shadowing dataset name.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, os, hypertools as hyp
os.chdir('/tmp')
arr = np.arange(12.0).reshape(4, 3)
hyp.save(arr, 'iris')
print(type(hyp.load('iris')))   # DataFrame with sklearn iris columns, NOT arr
print(np.array_equal(hyp.load('./iris'), arr))  # True -- workaround
findings.expected: Round-tripping a file you just saved returns your data, or save()/load() warns about the name collision.
findings.actual: SHADOWED: load('iris') returned DataFrame (cols ['sepal length (cm)', 'sepal width (cm)', 'petal length (cm)']) instead of the saved array; load('./iris') returns saved array: True | SHADOWED: load('weights') returned the hosted dataset (list of 36 arrays) instead of the saved array

findings.title: hyp.save crashes on the return of hyp.plot(animate=True) (HyperAnimation) with a cryptic internal error
findings.description: hyp.plot(..., animate=True) returns a HyperAnimation, and the io/save.py module docstring says a figure passed to save 'is pickled like any other object' -- but a HyperAnimation is not picklable: hyp.save(anim, 'anim.pkl') raises AttributeError naming the internal local function '_draw.<locals>.update_lines_parallel', with no hint that the supported export path is anim.save('anim.gif') or hyp.plot(..., save_path=...). Combined with F20-save-001, if the target file already existed it is also destroyed by the failed attempt. A type check with a friendly redirect (or making the error name the fix) would resolve this. Static-figure saves are fine: the pickled hyp.plot Figure round-trips with pixel-identical re-render (evidence PNGs), and plotly figures round-trip with semantically identical JSON.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
import matplotlib; matplotlib.use('Agg')
data = np.random.RandomState(42).randn(60, 4).cumsum(axis=0)
anim = hyp.plot(data, animate=True, show=False, duration=2, frame_rate=5)
hyp.save(anim, '/tmp/anim.pkl')  # AttributeError
findings.expected: Either a picklable animation handle, or a clear error: 'HyperAnimation objects cannot be pickled; use anim.save("file.gif"/"file.mp4") or hyp.plot(..., save_path=...) to export.'
findings.actual: RAISED AttributeError: Can't get local object '_draw.<locals>.update_lines_parallel'

findings.title: save() accepts **kwargs but silently ignores all of them (protocol=, compression=, typos)
findings.description: save(obj, fname, **kwargs) swallows every keyword argument without effect or warning. Verified: hyp.save(arr, f, protocol=0) still writes a protocol-4 pickle (header b'\x80\x04' identical to the default -- a protocol-0 pickle would be ASCII); compression='gzip' writes an uncompressed pickle (magic b'\x80\x04', not gzip's b'\x1f\x8b'); typo kwargs (fnme='oops.pkl', overwrite=False) are accepted silently. A user who explicitly requests protocol=2 for compatibility with an older Python silently gets protocol 4/5 files that their target environment may not read. Either forward kwargs to pickle.dump (protocol/fix_imports/buffer_callback are the natural ones) or drop **kwargs so typos raise TypeError.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
hyp.save(np.arange(5), '/tmp/p0.pkl', protocol=0)
print(open('/tmp/p0.pkl', 'rb').read(2))  # b'\x80\x04' -- protocol arg ignored
hyp.save(np.arange(5), '/tmp/gz.pkl', compression='gzip', fnme='typo')  # no error
findings.expected: protocol= forwarded to pickle.dump (file starts with protocol-0 ASCII opcodes); unknown kwargs raise TypeError.
findings.actual: default file header=b'\x80\x04', protocol=0 file header=b'\x80\x04' -> identical=True | compression='gzip' accepted without error; file magic=b'\x80\x04' | typo kwargs fnme= and overwrite=False accepted silently, no error

findings.title: save() does not expand '~' or environment variables although load() does (asymmetric path handling)
findings.description: load() applies expanduser(expandvars(...)) to paths, but save() passes fname straight to open(). Verified: hyp.save(arr, '~/f.pkl') raises FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '~/hypertools_f20_tilde_test.pkl', and hyp.save(arr, '$F20DIR/envvar.pkl') likewise -- while hyp.load resolves both forms. So the natural pair save(x, '~/data.pkl') / load('~/data.pkl') fails on the save half. (If a literal '~' directory exists in cwd, the file would even be written there, diverging from where load looks.) One-line fix: open(os.path.expanduser(os.path.expandvars(fname)), 'wb') for str/bytes fnames.
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
hyp.save(np.arange(3), '~/f20_tilde.pkl')  # FileNotFoundError; hyp.load('~/f20_tilde.pkl') would have expanded
findings.expected: save() resolves '~' and '$VARS' exactly like load() so save/load pairs are symmetric.
findings.actual: save('~/...') RAISED FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '~/hypertools_f20_tilde_test.pkl' | save('$F20DIR/...') RAISED FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '$F20DIR/envvar.pkl'

findings.title: save() docstring is a single line: no Parameters/Returns/Examples, **kwargs undocumented, and the Sphinx API page inherits the bare line
findings.description: help(hyp.save) renders in full as: "save(obj, fname, **kwargs)\n    Pickle `obj` to `fname`." -- no numpydoc sections, no statement of accepted obj types, no overwrite/truncation semantics, no round-trip example, no pointer to hyp.load or to plot(save_path=)/HyperAnimation.save for figure export, and no mention of what **kwargs does (nothing -- F20-save-005). Every sibling public API function (load, plot, reduce, align...) carries a full numpydoc docstring; docs/hypertools.save.rst autofunctions save, so the rendered API page for hypertools.save shows only this line. Also note the important pickle-security caveat lives only in the module docstring, which autofunction does not render. There are no docstring examples to execute (verified), so the release docs ship a public function with effectively no documentation.

import hypertools as hyp, pydoc
print(pydoc.render_doc(hyp.save, renderer=pydoc.plaintext))
findings.expected: Numpydoc docstring with Parameters (obj, fname), Returns (None), overwrite/truncate semantics, security note, a save->load example, and a See Also pointing at load / plot(save_path=).

findings.title: Stale module-docstring NOTE: says the format-aware figure exporter 'comes later' / 'lands in Plan 6', but it has already landed
findings.description: hypertools/io/save.py's module docstring states: 'NOTE: figure/animation export (png/pdf/svg/html/gif/mp4) is NOT handled here -- it depends on the plot backends and lands in Plan 6 (plot). A figure passed here is pickled like any other object; the format-aware exporter comes later.' The exporter now exists: hyp.plot has save_path= in its signature, and HyperAnimation.save's docstring says the writer 'is chosen by file extension -- gif and png/apng ... matching what hyp.plot(..., save_path=...) supports.' The forward-looking planning language ('Plan 6', 'comes later') is stale for a 1.0 release and should instead point users at the existing export paths.
findings.expected: Module note reads e.g.: 'figure/animation export is handled by hyp.plot(..., save_path=...) and HyperAnimation.save(); a figure passed here is pickled instead.'
findings.actual: save.py lines 7-9: 'it depends on the plot backends and lands in Plan 6 (plot). A figure passed here is pickled like any other object; the format-aware exporter comes later.' -- while plot.py line ~172 already has 'save_path=None' and hyper_animation.py implements extension-driven save().

findings.title: No format-aware saving despite format-rich load: save cannot write CSV/npy/parquet/etc., and does not create missing parent directories
findings.description: hyp.load parses .npy/.npz/.csv/.tsv/.txt/.json/.parquet/.mat/.xlsx/.xls plus pickles, but hyp.save can only pickle -- there is no extension dispatch, so users must fall back to pandas/numpy for interoperable outputs, and any extension they pass is misleading (F20-save-002). Additionally, saving into a nonexistent nested directory raises a bare FileNotFoundError ('[Errno 2] No such file or directory: .../a/b/c/x.pkl') rather than creating parents (a makedirs(exist_ok=True) or a friendlier message would help scientists writing results into new output trees). Suggested 1.x enhancement: extension-driven writers mirroring load's readers, parent-directory creation (or an opt-in mkdir=True), and atomic writes (F20-save-001).
findings.repro:
import numpy as np, hypertools as hyp
hyp.save(np.arange(3), '/tmp/f20_new_dir/a/b/x.pkl')  # FileNotFoundError, no mkdir
# and no way to produce a real CSV: hyp.save(df, 'x.csv') pickles (see F20-save-002)
findings.expected: save(df, 'x.csv') writes real CSV (etc., mirroring load), and/or parent directories are created.
findings.actual: RAISED FileNotFoundError: [Errno 2] No such file or directory: '/private/tmp/.../t03_files/a/b/c/x.pkl'; all extensions produce pickle bytes (magic b'\x80\x04')

findings.title: Shipped test suite never round-trips hyp.save through hyp.load
findings.description: tests/io/test_save.py contains only two tests: one saves an array and reloads it with raw pickle.load (not hyp.load), the other only checks hyp.save is callable and the file exists. No shipped test covers the save->hyp.load round-trip, DataFrame/index/dtype fidelity, list-of-arrays, or any failure path -- the pairing that this audit exercised (and where the shadowing and data-loss behaviors live) is untested. Not a runtime defect; filed for release-hardening visibility.
